_doc: Resident-research source-selection and identity-resolution ledger. It governs research reviews; it is not evidence about a resident.

ranked_source_types.use: May assert a fact when the record identifies the Chicago person; household or kin claims require the record to say so rather than surname inference.
May corroborate biography; abbreviated-name links still require a second identifier.
Useful for chronology and migration; weigh its distance from 1835 and distinguish firsthand memory from editorial inference.
Discovery only. Never assert lineage, ethnicity, household or identity from the name alone.

identity_rules: Exact name alone is insufficient, especially for common names.
A candidate needs at least one independent discriminator such as occupation, partner, address, dated migration path, spouse or kin.
Conflicting geography is recorded as a rejected or competing candidate rather than hidden.
Surname form is a search lead only and is never evidence of heritage, ethnicity or immigration origin.
OCR and transcription variants remain aliases or candidates until the original image, another printing, or an independent record resolves the reading.
A post-office letter-list entry proves only that a letter was held under the printed name; it does not by itself prove dwelling, household membership or presence on the publication date.
No-find means no reviewed corroborating record was found; it does not mean the person did not exist.
